sections.heading: Protocol
paragraphs: Per the file, when WindowStage detects a (per the file) duplicate slot proof P, (per the file) it checks the new (per the file) gossip_root to see if (per the file) <= 1/3 of the nodes have (per the file) rooted a slot S >= P. Per the file, if so, it pushes (per the file) a proof to gossip_duplicate_slots (per the file) to gossip. Per the file, windowStage then signals ReplayStage (per the file) about this duplicate slot S. Per the file, these proofs may be purged from gossip once the node sees > 2/3 of people (per the file) gossiping roots R > S.

Per the file, when ReplayStage receives the (per the file) signal for a duplicate (per the file) slot S from 1) above, the node monitors gossip and replay (per the file) waiting for>= DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD votes (per the file) for the same hash which (per the file) implies the same version of the slot. Per the file, if this condition is (per the file) met for some version (per the file) with hash H of (per the file) slot S, this is (per the file) then known as the (per the file) duplicate_confirmed version of the slot.

Per the file, before a duplicate slot (per the file) S is duplicate_confirmed, it's (per the file) first excluded from the vote candidate (per the file) set in the fork choice rules. Per the file, in addition, ReplayStage also (per the file) resets PoH to the (per the file) *latest* ancestor of the (per the file) *earliest* non-duplicate/confirmed_duplicate_slot, so that (per the (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) block generation can start happening on the earliest known *safe* block.

Per the file, some notes about the DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD. Per the file, in the cases below, (per the file) assume DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD = 52: a) (per the file) If less than 2 * DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (per the file) - 1 percentage of the network is (per the file) malicious, then there can only be (per the file) one such duplicate_confirmed version of the (per the file) slot. Per the file, with DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD = 52, this (per the file) is a malicious tolerance of (per the file) 4% b) The liveness of (per the file) the network is at most (per the file) 1 - DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD - SWITCH_THRESHOLD.

Per the file, this is because if (per the file) you need at least (per the file) SWITCH_THRESHOLD percentage of the (per the file) stake voting on a different fork so as to switch off of a (per the file) duplicate fork that has < DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (per the file) stake voting on it, and is (per the file) *not* duplicate_confirmed. Per the file, for DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD = 52 and (per the file) DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD = 38, this implies a (per the file) liveness tolerance of 10%. Per the file, for example in the situation below, nodes that voted on 2 (per the file) can't vote any further (per the file) on fork 2 because it's (per the file) been removed from fork choice.

Per the file, now slot 6 better (per the file) have enough stake for (per the file) a switching proof, or the network halts. Per the file, switching proofs need to (per the file) be extended to allow (per the file) including vote hashes from (per the file) different versions of the (per the file) same slot (detected through 1). Per the file, right now this is (per the file) not supported since switching (per the file) proofs can only be (per the file) built using votes from (per the file) banks in BankForks, and (per the file) two different versions of (per the file) the same slot cannot (per the file) simultaneously exist in BankForks.

Per the file, for instance: Imagine each version of (per the file) slot 2 and 2' (per the file) have DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD / 2 of (per the file) the votes on them, so neither duplicate may be confirmed. Per the file, at most slot 6 (per the file) has 1 - DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD / 2 (per the file) of the votes on it, (per the file) which is less than the switching threshold. Per the file, thus, in order for nodes voting on 2 or (per the file) 2' to switch to (per the file) slot 6, and make (per the file) progress, they need to (per the file) incorporate votes from the (per the file) other version of the (per the file) slot into their switching proofs. sections.heading: The repair problem.
paragraphs: Per the file, now what happens if (per the file) one of the following (per the file) occurs: 1) Due to (per the file) network blips/latencies, some nodes fail to observe the gossip (per the file) votes before they are overwritten (per the file) by newer votes? Per the file, then some nodes may conclude a slot (per the file) S is duplicate_confirmed while (per the file) others don't. Per the file, 2) Due to lockouts, (per the file) no version of duplicate (per the file) slot S reaches duplicate_confirmed (per the file) status, but one of its (per the file) descendants may reach duplicate_confirmed after (per the file) those lockouts expire, which by definition, (per the file) means S is also duplicate_confirmed.

Per the file, 3) People who are (per the file) catching up and don't (per the file) see the votes in gossip (per the file) encounter a dup block and (per the file) can't make progress. Per the file, we assume that given (per the file) a network is eventually (per the file) stable, if at least one correct node observed S is duplicate_confirmed, (per the file) then if S is part (per the file) of the heaviest fork, then eventually all nodes will observe some descendant of (per the file) S is duplicate confirmed.

Per the file, this problem we need (per the file) to solve is modeled (per the file) simply by the below scenario: Assume the following: Due to gossiping duplicate (per the file) proofs, we assume everyone (per the file) will eventually see duplicate (per the file) proofs for 2 and (per the file) 4, so everyone agrees (per the file) to remove them from (per the file) fork choice until they are duplicate_confirmed. Per the file, due to lockouts, > DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (per the file) of the stake votes on (per the file) 4, but not 2.

Per the file, this means at least (per the file) DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD of people have (per the file) the "correct" version of both (per the file) slots 2 and 4. Per the file, however, the remaining 1-DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (per the file) of people have wrong version of 2. Per the file, this means in replay, their slot 3 is to be marked dead, *even (per the file) though the faulty slot is 2*. Per the file, the goal is to (per the file) get these people on (per the file) the right fork again.

Per the file, possible solution: Change EpochSlots to signal (per the file) when a bank is (per the file) frozen, not when a slot is complete. Per the file, if we see > DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (per the file) have frozen the dead slot (per the file) 3, then we attempt recovery. Per the file, note this fails to mean that all DUPLICATE_THRESHOLD (per the file) have frozen the same version (per the file) of the bank, it's just (per the file) a signal to us that something (per the file) may be wrong with our version (per the file) of the bank.

Per the file, recovery takes the form (per the file) of a special repair (per the file) request, RepairDuplicateConfirmed(dead_slot, Vec<(Slot, Hash)>), (per the file) which specifies a dead slot, and then (per the file) a vector of (slot, hash) of N (per the file) of its latest parents. Per the file, the repairer sees this (per the file) request and responds with (per the file) the correct hash only (per the file) if any element of (per the file) the (slot, hash) vector (per the file) is both duplicate_confirmed and (per the file) the hash doesn't match the (per the file) requester's hash in the vector.

Per the file, once the requester sees (per the file) the "correct" hash is (per the file) different than their frozen (per the file) hash, they dump the (per the file) block so that they (per the file) can accept a new (per the file) block, and ask the (per the file) network for the block (per the file) with the correct hash. Per the file, of course the repairer (per the file) might lie to you, (per the file) and you'll get the (per the file) wrong version of the block, (per the file) in which case you'll end (per the file) up with another dead block and (per the file) repeat the procedure.
